title: Membership in the coordinate-swapped set
statement: Let $R \subseteq X \times Y$, and write $\mathrm{swap}(R) = \{(y,x) \mid (x,y) \in R\} \subseteq Y \times X$ for the set obtained by exchanging the two coordinates of every element of $R$. Then for any pair $(y, x) \in Y \times X$, one has $(y, x) \in \mathrm{swap}(R)$ if and only if $(x, y) \in R$.
hypotheses_covered: $R$ is a set of pairs in $X \times Y$
replaced:
For any set $R \subseteq X \times Y$ and pair $(y, x) \in Y \times X$,
$(y, x) \in \texttt{swapInputSet}(R)$ if and only if $(x, y) \in R$.
